item.title: Ex-Cambridge professor dies week after resigning amid plagiarism allegations
item.description: Jason Arday, who was Cambridge's youngest Black professor, died in London on Friday, the school said.

item.title: Army temporarily grounds Apache helicopter training flights after deadly crash
item.description: The U.S. Army said Friday it is temporarily halting Apache helicopter training flights after two soldiers were killed earlier this week​ in a crash near Fort Hood, Texas.

item.title: What to know after Luigi Mangione pleads guilty in federal case to killing UnitedHealthcare CEO
item.description: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty on Friday to federal charges for the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson joins with analysis.

item.title: Trial of man accused of ordering Tupac Shakur's killing set to begin Monday
item.description: The trial for the former gang leader accused of ordering Tupac Shakur's 1996 murder will begin Monday. Attorney Chris Melcher joins CBS News to discuss the case.

item.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty in federal case, admits to shooting Brian Thompson
item.description: Luigi Mangione entered a guilty plea in his federal case at a court appearance in Manhattan Friday morning.

item.title: FBI: Violent crime plummeted in 2025, murder rate hit 20-year low
item.description: The White House is touting a historic drop in violent crime as the FBI releases the latest data from its annual Uniform Crime Reporting Program.

item.title: Hawaii under a hurricane warning as Tropical Storm Lala takes aim
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala could bring heavy rain, high winds and dangerous surf and rip currents to the Hawaiian Islands as a hurricane this weekend, forecasters say.

item.title: Russian tanker leaking oil off Oman coast, threatening environmental disaster
item.description: The Caroline Bezengi, linked to Russia's so-called shadow fleet, is carrying millions of gallons of oil and has run aground off the coast of Oman.

item.title: Justice Department expands military's power to detain migrants near border
item.description: The Justice Department issued a legal opinion giving the U.S. military broader powers to detain migrants near certain areas along the southern border.

item.title: Satellite images of sunken Russian tanker off Oman coast show growing oil slick
item.description: An abandoned Russian tanker carrying millions of gallons of oil off the coast of Oman could potentially cause a larger environmental disaster after it was damaged from an unexplained explosion in early June. Satellite images show a growing oil slick in the area. Here's what to know.

item.title: Trump says U.S. warship's 9-month deployment "not nearly long enough"
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln has been deployed for almost nine months and is expected to be replaced in the Middle East.

item.title: USS Washington aircraft carrier heads to Middle East to replace USS Lincoln
item.description: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier departed Vietnam last week and is headed to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, according to a U.S. official.

item.title: Hormuz chaos highlights risks for other global trade chokepoints
item.description: The war in Iran has underscored how disruptions to a key shipping route thousands of miles away can have a material impact on American consumers.

item.title: FDA upgrades egg recall linked to salmonella to highest risk level
item.description: U.S. food regulators say 1.6 million cartons of recalled eggs can "cause serious adverse health consequences or death."

item.title: Where the Texas surrogate dispute stands right now
item.description: The legal fight over who has parental rights to a baby in the middle of a surrogacy dispute is playing out in Texas. Rachel Rebouché, professor of law at the University of Texas School of Law, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Golfer Jessica Bang, 18, dies while preparing for tournament in Thailand
item.description: Jessica Bang collapsed on Aug. 1 as she was preparing in Thailand for a tournament and was transported to a hospital in Bangkok.

item.title: Marine vet on USS Lincoln's 200+ days without port call: "Very abnormal number"
item.description: Jonathan Simkins, editor-in-chief of the Military Times and a Marine Corps veteran, joins CBS News 24/7 to share his thoughts on the reports of poor conditions on the ship and the crew's record-setting deployment.

item.title: Paintings worth $10 million that were stolen in 3-minute heist are recovered
item.description: The recovered works are valued at more than $10 million.

item.title: How double jeopardy could come into play after Mangione guilty plea
item.description: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to two federal counts on Friday. His state trial is currently scheduled to begin on Sept. 8.

item.title: How to get a refund for Trump tariffs struck down by Supreme Court
item.description: The U.S. has refunded more than $100 billion in illegal tariffs to businesses, and some of that money is going to consumers — here's what to know.

item.title: Walmart tomato soup kits recalled over Listeria risk, FDA says
item.description: The 14oz soup kits were distributed at Walmart stores in 29 states between June 30 and July 7, according to the FDA.

item.title: See how much renters pay for a 2-bedroom home in 50 U.S. cities

item.title: Indiana river breaks 1913 flooding record as governor declares state of emergency
item.description: The White River in Indiana rose to record-breaking levels as more than 11 inches of rain has fallen east of Indianapolis since Tuesday.

item.title: Flock CEO responds to abuses of its surveillance technology

item.title: Baby in surrogate dispute now in custody of parents, lawyer says
item.description: The baby at the center of a surrogacy dispute was born in Texas Wednesday and has hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a rare heart defect.

item.title: My husband was kicked out of hospice. Here's what I learned.
item.description: Some seriously ill patients improve on hospice. About 1 in 16 patients enrolled in hospice care lose eligibility as a result. Here's how to get appropriate care.

item.title: Saturday Sessions: GA-20 and Charlie Musselwhite perform "I Can't Hold Out"
item.description: Grammy-winning harmonica virtuoso Charlie Musselwhite is a pioneer of the 60s Chicago blues scene. GA-20 and Charlie Musselwhite join forces for an electrifying blues collaboration, culminating in their new album "Blues Now!"
